decision: Bounded AI after manual command stability
No DWG promise in early releases

Project access gates use the single workspace role (owner/administrator/editor/commenter/viewer) uniformly across every project in that workspace; no per-project ACL in v1 - external per-project access goes through share_link tokens instead

OPEN - who can resolve a comment or change an issue's status/assignee: the same role that can create one (commenter+), or does resolving/reassigning require editor+? RBAC-MATRIX.csv deliberately leaves this unanswered rather than guessing.

OPEN - ENTITLEMENT-MATRIX-DRAFT.csv gates 'Roles and approvals' to team/enterprise tiers only, but the DB schema's workspace_role enum and RBAC-MATRIX.csv (invite_member/change_role) are not tier-scoped anywhere - does a free/professional-tier owner get invite_member/change_role at all, or only a single implicit owner-only workspace with no distinct roles? This needs a business decision, not an assumption.

OPEN (= ARQ-058, ADR-0004) - canonical internal unit representation for stored geometry: millimetres vs metres vs another base unit, and fixed-point/integer vs floating-point numeric representation. Every geometry/editor module built so far (packages/geometry-2d's coordinate-system.ts, packages/editor-shell's viewport-controller.ts and every snap-*.ts, packages/editor-shell's metric/imperial numeric-input parsers) explicitly treats this as unresolved and uses plain floating-point numbers as a provisional, easily-swappable choice - none of them should be read as this decision having been made. Needs an explicit engineering decision (precision/rounding requirements, interop with DWG/IFC importers, floating-point accumulation error over large plans) before ADR-0004 can move out of 'Research required'.
